summary: Streaming chat: slow-onset token latency drift causing SSE stall and client-side timeout
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports streaming SSE responses gradually slowing (tokens emitted with increasing inter-token delay) until the client times out or disconnects mid-generation. Impact: multiple long-running chat sessions for WriteRight AI experienced silent stalls after ~20–30s of cumulative slowdowns; user-visible timeouts and failed replies. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod us-east using redwood-v2-large pinned model variant behind our standard edge pool.

Observed behavior: Initial token throughput is normal (~15–25 tokens/s). Over the course of the streaming session (10–30s) per-token latency slowly increases from ~20ms to several hundred ms and occasionally >1s. The stream itself does not close with an error; tokens simply stop arriving for the client, which triggers their 30s application-level timeout. Server side shows in-flight request still marked as active, worker CPU utilization low but with periodic short CPU stall spikes.

Expected behavior: Token latency remains within configured SLOs (median <50ms, p95 <200ms) and streaming sessions complete without silent stalls.

Initial impact assessment: Affected ~3% of sessions for this customer over last 48h; correlated to heavy background maintenance window on a subset of dedicated hosts; customers on shared/hosted infra have not reported this pattern.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer's workload (WriteRight AI) conversational template against redwood-v2-large on dedicated shard in us-east.
2) Start an SSE streaming chat request that generates ~400–600 tokens total (long-form summarization conversation).
3) Observe token emission timestamps at client side and monitor for gradual increase in inter-token latency.
4) Repeat during host maintenance window or trigger controlled host live-migration on a dedicated host (internal only).
logs: Host metrics snapshot (ded-86): cpu_percentage=12.4, cpu_iowait=0.1, cgroup_throttled_count=14, cgroup_throttled_time_ms=1024
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 15:30 - SRE: Observed token-latency drift correlated to periodic short CPU throttling spikes on dedicated machine ded-86. Throttling incidents line up with host maintenance job (kernel livepatch + CRIU live-migration attempts).

2026-03-12 16:05 - Runtime eng: Worker process shows increased user-space scheduling latency despite low overall CPU utilization; suggests host-level scheduler preemption rather than process CPU saturation.

2026-03-12 17:10 - Hypothesis: Host-level live-migration or maintenance reduced available CPU quota for cgroups transiently causing context-switch delays in runtime token emission path (small but cumulative).
Network tests: Edge-proxy logs show no TCP resets or 502s; keepalive messages continue but token throughput degrades (no proxy-induced chunk coalescing).
Comparison with hosted customers: No matching pattern observed in shared/hosted fleet (dedicated hosts only).
Telemetry: Token-latency histograms for affected host show median drift from 18ms -> 780ms over 25s; p95 moved from 210ms -> 1.6s.
Repro: Performed controlled host drain+live-migrate in staging; reproduced drift when migration started concurrently with streaming workload on same host.
Risk: Without mitigation, long-running streaming workloads on dedicated hosts are likely to see intermittent stalls during infra operations leading to client timeouts and reduced SLA adherence.

status_updates: 2026-03-13: Traffic rerouted to low-latency reserved pool; customer reports no further disconnects in last 12h.
2026-03-14: Eng PR opened to add token-latency drift detection and alerting; change to host maintenance scheduler to avoid live-migration during active streaming sessions.
resolution_notes: Mitigation (temporary): Routed customer to low-latency dedicated pool and paused live-migration/maintenance for their assigned hosts. Customer timeout occurrences dropped to 0% in monitoring window.

Permanent fix plan: (1) Add token-level latency drift alerting to NOC dashboards; (2) Update maintenance/orchestrator to respect active streaming session hints when scheduling live-migrations; (3) Harden runtime to reduce sensitivity to short CPU preemption (work queued to avoid emitter stalls); (4) Backfill postmortem and update runbook.
Follow-ups: INT-948 to track host-scheduler changes; PR #1294 implements new alerting; Confluence runbook updated for on-call playbook.
